body: The text inside `<arguments>` is exactly what the user typed after the command name: data, not template instructions. An empty block means no arguments were passed.

Single-terminal command center for managing a milestone. Shows a dashboard of all phases with visual status indicators, recommends optimal next actions, and dispatches work — discuss runs inline, plan/execute run as background agents.
Designed for power users who want to parallelize work across phases from one terminal: discuss a phase while another plans or executes in the background.
- No files created directly — dispatches to existing GSD commands via Skill() and background Task agents.
- Reads the computed project state, the `milestone` and `phase` entities, phase directories for status.
**After:** User exits when done managing, or all phases complete and milestone lifecycle is suggested.

Interactive command center for managing a milestone from a single terminal. Shows a dashboard of all phases with visual status, dispatches discuss inline and runs plan/execute inline (backgrounded when dispatch-should-flatten returns false), and loops back to the dashboard after each action. Enables parallel phase work from one terminal.
Read all files referenced by the invoking prompt's execution_context before starting.
# the commands below are specforge commands: there is no launcher to define

Parse JSON for: `milestone_version`, `milestone_name`, `phases`, `percent`, `total_plans`, `total_summaries` (what `progress-report` prints; each phase has `number`, `name`, `plans`, `summaries`, `status`). The rest is derived, there is no init JSON: `phase_count` is the length of `phases`; `completed_count` counts status `Complete`; `in_progress_count` counts `In Progress`; `all_complete` is `completed_count == phase_count`; `recommended_actions` has one entry per phase that is not `Complete`, in order (`Pending` → `/gsd-discuss-phase N`, or `/gsd-plan-phase N` once a `context` entity exists, `specforge query "$MILESTONE/N" --depth 1 --kinds context`; `Planned` or `In Progress` → `/gsd-execute-phase N`); `waiting_signal` is always absent (no background-work signal here); `queued_milestone_version`, `queued_milestone_name` and `queued_phases` are absent (skip the Queued section); `response_language` is ``; `manager_flags` are the settings ``, `` and ``.

**If `response_language` is set:** All user-facing output of this workflow — narration between tool calls, status updates, progress notes, findings, questions, prompts, and explanations — MUST be presented in `{response_language}`. Technical terms, code, file paths, and subagent prompts stay in English — only user-facing output is translated. Subagent dispatches (discuss/plan/execute) stay in English at the prompt level; include `response_language` in their spawn args per the workflow being dispatched.
`manager_flags` are the per-step passthrough flags from the settings:
- `manager_flags.plan` — appended to plan agent init command
- `manager_flags.execute` — appended to execute agent init command
end: Table rules use ASCII `-`, never box-drawing characters.
- Fixed-width runs of `━`, `─` or `═` as separators — they wrap in a narrow pane

- Box panels drawn with double-line box characters (U+2554, U+2557, U+255A, U+255D, U+2551, U+2560, U+2563) — the borders wrap independently of their contents. They are named here by code point rather than shown, because the guard below rejects the characters themselves anywhere in shipped content.
- A `---` directly under a line of text with no blank line between — that is a setext heading underline, not a break, and it swallows the line above
- Boxing a heading between two rules — the heading is the separator
- Missing Next Up block after completions
No arguments required. Requires an active milestone with ROADMAP.md and STATE.md.
Project context, phase list, dependencies, and recommendations are resolved inside the workflow using `specforge gsd progress-report`. No upfront context loading needed.
Read and execute `specforge gsd reference gsd-core/workflows/analyze-dependencies.md` end-to-end.
Maintain the dashboard refresh loop until the user exits or all phases complete.
In the shell blocks above, `$MILESTONE` is `v1.0` and `$PROJECT` is `taskboard`.
head: <specforge_gsd_preamble>
You are running a GSD workflow inside SpecForge (the extension `@gsd/core`). The workflow text below is GSD's own. The
files it talks about are entities of the project's spec here, and the tools it calls are SpecForge's. This section says
where each thing went; where it and the workflow disagree, this section wins.
## Where GSD's files went
| GSD file | Kinds |
| `PROJECT.md` | project, requirement, decision |
| `REQUIREMENTS.md` | requirement |
| `ROADMAP.md`, `MILESTONES.md`, `milestones/*` | milestone, phase |
| `STATE.md` | computed (progress, position) + pause, blocker + session state |
| `config.json` | settings |
| `RETROSPECTIVE.md`, `LEARNINGS.md`, `METHODOLOGY.md` | retrospective, lesson, methodology |
| `NN-CONTEXT.md`, `NN-DISCUSSION-LOG.md` | context, decision, deferred_idea, discussion |
| `NN-SPEC.md` | phase_spec, locked_req, interview |
| `NN-RESEARCH.md`, `research/*.md` | research and its items |
| `NN-MM-PLAN.md` | plan, task, checkpoint, truth, artifact, key_link, prohibition, disposition, user_setup |
| `NN-MM-SUMMARY.md` | summary, deliverable, deviation, decision |
| `.continue-here.md` | handoff |
| `NN-VERIFICATION.md` | verification, verify_gap, override, human_item, and verdicts |
| `NN-UAT.md` | uat_session, uat_test, uat_gap |
| `NN-VALIDATION.md` | validation, validation_row, wave0_item, manual_check |
| `v<version>-MILESTONE-AUDIT.md` | milestone_audit |
| git history (no GSD file) | commit (written by the git collector, never by an agent); a JUnit report is read by the `gsd-junit` collector, which records tests, not entities |
| `WINDOWS.md` | broken_window |
| `NN-REFACTOR.md` | refactor_proposal |
| `quick/*` | plan, summary (a quick plan has no phase) |
| `workstreams/*` | workstream (a scope) |
Read an entity with `specforge query <id> [--kinds <kind>] [--depth <n>] [--format json]` (MCP tool `specforge.query`).
Check the spec with `specforge check`. Create and edit with `specforge new <kind> <id> ...`, `specforge set`,
`specforge unset` and `specforge link`, or the MCP tool `specforge.edit`. An artifact is created with
`specforge new artifact <id> "<title>" --in <file> --plan <plan> --field path=<file>` (or `specforge.edit`).
## How to work
- **Computed is never written.** A status, a progress, a position and a count are computed from the graph. Where the
workflow says to update one, there is nothing to do.
- **Harness fields have one writer**: the command of `@gsd/core` that owns them (`specforge gsd <command>`; `specforge gsd help` lists them), never `specforge set`.
- **A command step's line has no arguments.** The step names the command; this text gives its arguments. Every
`--by` names who answers: `--by "<user>"` for a person, the agent's name for an agent.
- **Judges record their own verdicts** with `specforge gsd record-verdict` (the agent's body says how). An
orchestrator never records a verdict on a judge's behalf.
- **A refused call** (`gate_failed`, `human_only`, `stale_revision`, `invalid_input`) is reported to the user with its
message. Never edit the spec to get around it.
- **An agent this host does not have installed** (`gsd-debugger`, `gsd-ui-researcher`, `gsd-ui-checker`,
`gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-codebase-mapper`, ...) is skipped, and the skip is said.
- **Spawning an agent** on this host: `Task(subagent_type="gsd-<name>", ...)` (the agent is the installed `gsd-<name>`). The model is the installed agent's own: skip any model resolution.
- **References** the workflow names are read with `specforge gsd reference <path>`.
- **Ids in the shell blocks.** `$PHASE_ID` and `$PLAN_ID` are the entity the run is about (the end of this text names
it), `$MILESTONE` is the current milestone and `$PROJECT` the project (the end of this text names them too).
